newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - Sept 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - Sept 3.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Telephone: 11-3324842, 11-3761233; Fax: 91-11-3351006 Internet : biznis.news@forums.sprintrpg.sprint.com
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
PRIME MINISTER MAY TAKE UPPER HOUSE ROUTE TO PARLIAMENT

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda may not contest elections for the Lok Sabha (Lower house of parliament) for gaining membership of the Parliament. Gowda who was sworn in as Prime Minister on June 1 has to become a member of either House of Parliament within six months. Earlier he had said he would contest the Lok Sabha election from Hassan in Karnataka. However, sources say he plans to enter the Parliament by getting elected to the Upper House. The Election Commission's list for byelections to be held for Lok Sabha, which was declared today, does not include Hassan, the place from where Gowda wanted to contest.
The Hindustan Times
ILLEGAL MONEY TRANSFER CASE PROGRESS NOT SATISFACTORY

The Supreme Court expressed its unhappiness over the probe being conducted by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) into the hawala, or illegal money transfer, case. The Court said the CBI had gone soft on the main accused in the scam in which country's top politicians allegedly received hundreds of thousands of rupees as bribe from a hawala operator. The Court criticised the CBI for failing to file criminal charges against the main accused. The Court asked the CBI to assure that it would speed up action on the matter.
The Times Of India
CONGRESS CHIEF REJECTS PARTY MEETING ON CORRUPTION

Congress party president P.V. Narasimha Rao rejected a demand for a general body meeting (GBM) of the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) to exclusively discuss the issue of corruption. Some Congress Parliament members were said to have called upon Rao to convene a GBM of the CPP. Rao veered clear of the CPP meet as it could ultimately lead to the demand for a change in the leadership of the party, said sources. The GBM, due to be held on September 4, would discuss electoral reforms only, said a CPP spokesman.
The Economic Times
RPG POCKETS DHOLPUR POWER PROJECT, MODI GETS BARSINGAR

Hindustan Development Corp, a Modi Group company, bagged the multi-million rupee lignite-based Barsingar power project in Rajasthan. The state government awarded the multi-million rupee naphtha-based 770-MW Dholpur power project to RPG Enterprises. With the award of these projects, Rajasthan achieved a major breakthrough in attracting private sector investments in the state's power sector.
FOREIGN INVESTMENT HITS A LOW AT 2.36 BLN RUPEES

Net monthly investments by foreign institutional investors (FIIS) have hit an all time low in the curent year. The investment totalled just 2.37 billion rupees until August 29, 1996, according to figures available with the Securities and Exchange Board of India. Market sources say that net investments for the whole of August may not exceed 3.0 billion rupees. The setback in funds inflow into the country comes after a gap of eight months as levels of investments into the country had been improving since it hit a low of 1.69 billion rupees in November last year.
Financial Express
UNIT TRUST MOOTS NEW THREE-TIER REVAMP PACKAGE

The Unit Trust of India (UTI) has decided to opt for a three-tiered restructuring package. It envisages complete segregation of the asset management and trusteeship functions. The restructuring package proposes one asset management company, which would hold stakes in other UTI subsidiaries, formation of a trust with distinct identity and formation of an associate company to be in charge of all other investment activities.
SHELL IN TALKS WITH MAFATLAL GROUP TO PICK UP STAKE

Anglo-Dutch major Royal Dutch Shell is reported to be in talks with the Mafatlal group for picking up a substantial equity stake in the National Organic Chemical Industries Ltd (NOCIL). Besides Shell, other international petrochemical majors such as U.S.-based Dow Chemicals and a Mitsubishi-led consortium are also negotiating with the Mafatlals for a sizeable equity stake in NOCIL. The size of the equity stake and the pricing were likely to be decided following a survey of NOCIL's facilities by the negotiators, sources said.
ESSAR OIL TO RAISE FUNDS IN GLOBAL MARKET

Essar Oil Ltd is planning an overseas equity issue of a maximum amount of $250 million. The company is setting up a nine million tonne refinery project at Jamnagar in Gujarat. Essar Oil's move to raise funds in the global market followed the continued weakness of the company's scrip in the domestic stockmarkets.
Business Standard
CRACKDOWN ON ILLEGAL CARRY FORWARD, SHORT SALES

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the bourse regulator, in a nationwide crackdown on illegal carry forward (badla) operations and short sales, issued show cause notices to 33 brokers at Pune, Calcutta and Mumbai. They include five elected directors of the Pune bourse and the vice-president of the Calcutta bourse. The governing board of the former was served with a show cause for violations by the bourse's elected directors. Most of the badla operations were found to have been linked to short sales. The bourse regulator has invoked the provisions of the SEBI Act, the SEBI Brokers' and Unfair Trade Practices Regulations for taking action.
STERLING CELLULAR FUNDING PLAN ON HOLD

The foreign investment promotion board (FIPB) has shelved Essar Telecom-controlled Sterling Cellular's request for routing the investment of Swiss PTT through the latter's fully owned subsidiary, Mobilevest. FIPB's decision was prompted by a request in this regard by the department of telecommunications (DoT). Swiss PTT was earlier allowed to take up 30 percent (90 million rupees) in Sterling Cellular. DoT was reviewing the proposal and was likely to decide on the matter later, DoT sources said.
INTEREST SUBSIDY FOR RURAL FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS PROPOSED

The agriculture minister has proposed an interest subsidy to rural financial institutions as part of measures to bring down the cost of short-term credit for farmers. The proposed two percent reduction in the interest on crop loans is estimated to involve a total subsidy of around four billion rupees a year.
The Observer
SUGAR, ALCOHOL DELICENSING SHELVED

The industry ministry's move to delicense industries, including sugar, alcohol and cigarette, has been grounded. This is being attributed to the political leadership's unwillingness to decide on the matter until the completion of assembly polls in Uttar Pradesh (UP). The government was averse to taking any decision before UP polls on sugar, alcohol and cigarette industries because they were considered politically sensitive, said sources.
CENTRE DECANALISES SUGAR EXPORT

The Union government has decided to decanalise the export of sugar. This is aimed at providing necessary incentives to sugar manufacturing units to produce quality sugar. Civil Supplies Minister Devendra Yadav declared on the floor of Rajya Sabha (Upper House of Parliament) that a bill to amend the Sugar Export Act of 1958 would be introduced during the current session of Parliament to decanalise exports. He said that decanalisation would help the sugar manufacturing units secure a place in the global export market.
Business Line
TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPMENT BOARD SET UP

The government has constituted a 10-member Technology Development Board (TDB) with the Secretary, Department of Science and Technology, as its chairman. The TDB has been provided with 300 million rupees for the current fiscal in the annual Budget for 1996/97 to encourage the development of the indigenous technologies and also broad-base the use of imported technologies and for further improvisation. Sources said the board would be replenished with funds from the five percent cess being levied on import of technology.
TELECOMMUNICATION BILL IN FOR MAJOR CHANGES

The government might effect wide ranging amendments in the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) Bill. The bill is to come up for discussion in Parliament shortly. The recent developments in the telecommunication sector are said to have forced the government to take a serious view of certain provisions of the Bill. Sources said amendments might be effected to provisions relating to the role of regulators in interconnect charges, advisory role of TRAI in licensing, consumer representation in TRAI and composition of TRAI itself.
